'''Andrew Knyazev''' is an American [[mathematician]]. He graduated from the [[MSU Faculty of Computational Mathematics and Cybernetics|Faculty of Computational Mathematics and Cybernetics]] of [[Moscow State University]] under the supervision of [[Evgenii Georgievich D'yakonov]] ({{langx|ru|[[:ru:Дьяконов, Евгений Георгиевич|Евгений Георгиевич Дьяконов]]}}) in 1981 and obtained his [[Kandidat nauk|PhD]] in [[Numerical analysis|Numerical Mathematics]] at the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] under the supervision of [[Vyacheslav Ivanovich Lebedev]] ({{langx|ru|[[:ru:Лебедев, Вячеслав Иванович|Вячеслав Иванович Лебедев]]}}) in 1985. He worked at the [[Kurchatov Institute]] between 1981–1983, and then to 1992 at the [https://www.inm.ras.ru/en/ Marchuk Institute of Numerical Mathematics] ({{langx|ru|[[:ru:Институт вычислительной математики имени Г. И. Марчука РАН]]}}) of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], headed by [[Gury Marchuk]] ({{langx|ru|[[:ru:Марчук, Гурий Иванович|Гурий Иванович Марчук]]}}).

From 1993–1994, Knyazev held a visiting position at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] of [[New York University]], collaborating with [[Olof B. Widlund]].<ref>{{Citation
  | last1 = Knyazev
  | first1 = Andrew
  | last2 = Widlund
  | first2 = Olof
  | title = Lavrentiev Regularization + Ritz Approximation = Uniform Finite Element Error Estimates for Differential Equations with Rough Coefficients
  | journal = Mathematics of Computation
  | volume = 72
  | issue = 241
  | pages = 17–40
  | year = 2003
  | doi = 10.1090/S0025-5718-01-01378-3
  | doi-access = free
  }}
</ref> From 1994 until retirement in 2014, he was a Professor of [[Mathematics]] at the [[University of Colorado Denver]], supported by the [[National Science Foundation]]<ref>[https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/piSearch.do?SearchType=piSearch&page=1&QueryText=&PIFirstName=Andrew&PILastName=Knyazev&PIInstitution=&PIState=&PIZip=&PICountry=&Restriction=0&Search=Search#results Knyazev's NSF awards]</ref> and [[United States Department of Energy]] grants. He was a recipient of the 2008 Excellence in Research Award,<ref>{{Citation
  | title = Andrew Knyazev. 2008 Excellence in Research and Creative Activities Award Winner
  | date = 1 May 2008
  | url = http://math.ucdenver.edu/local/facultyaward.shtml
  | access-date = 12 January 2016
  | archive-date = 8 September 2011
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110908224434/http://math.ucdenver.edu/local/facultyaward.shtml
  | url-status = dead
  }}</ref> the 2000 college Teaching Excellence Award, and a finalist of the CU President's Faculty Excellence Award for Advancing Teaching and Learning through Technology in 1999.<ref>{{Citation
  | last =  Goodland
  | first = Marianne
| title = President's Faculty Excellence Award for Advancing Teaching and Learning through Technology
  | journal = Silver & Gold Record
  | volume = XXIX
  | issue = 34
  | date = 6 May 1999
  | url = http://math.ucdenver.edu/~aknyazev/teaching/exc99/sg.html
  }}
</ref> 
He was awarded the title of Professor Emeritus at the [[University of Colorado Denver]]<ref>{{Citation
 | title = Professor Emeritus University of Colorado Denver
  | date = 6 January 2016
  | url = http://www.merl.com/news/award-20160106-1141
   }}
</ref> 
and named the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics#SIAM Fellows|Fellow]] Class of 2016<ref>{{Citation
 | title = Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (SIAM) Fellows Class of 2016
| date = 31 March 2016
  | url = http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2016
}}
</ref>
and 
[[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] [[American Mathematical Society#Fellows|Fellow]] Class of 2019.<ref>{{Citation
 | title = American Mathematical Society (AMS) Fellows Class of 2019
| date = 31 October 2018
  | url = https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/ams-fellows
}}
</ref>

From 2012–2018, Knyazev worked at the [[Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories]]<ref>[http://www.netlib.org/na-digest-html/12/v12n40.html#2 Andrew Knyazev moved to MERL, 2012]</ref>  on algorithms for image and video processing, data sciences, optimal control, and material sciences, resulting in dozens of publications and 13 patent applications.<ref>[http://www.merl.com/people/knyazev Knyazev's Website] at [[Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories]] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120182228/http://www.merl.com/people/knyazev |date=January 20, 2018 }}</ref> Since 2018, he contributed to numerical techniques in [[quantum computing]] at [https://www.zapatacomputing.com Zapata Computing], real-time embedded [[anomaly detection]] in [[automotive]] data, and algorithms for [[silicon photonics]]-based hardware.

Knyazev is mostly known for his work in numerical solution of large [[sparse matrix|sparse]] [[eigenvalue|eigenvalue problem]]s, particularly [[preconditioning]]<ref>{{Citation
  | last = Knyazev
  | first = A.V.
  | title = Preconditioned eigensolvers - an oxymoron?
  | journal = Electron. Trans. Numer. Anal.
  | volume = 7
  | pages = 104–123
  | year = 1998
  | url = http://www.emis.de/journals/ETNA/vol.7.1998/pp104-123.dir/pp104-123.pdf
  }}
</ref> and the iterative method [[LOBPCG]].<ref>{{Citation
  | last = Knyazev
  | first = A.V.
  | title = Toward the Optimal Preconditioned Eigensolver: Locally Optimal Block Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Method
  | journal = SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing
  | volume = 23
  | issue = 2
  | pages = 517–541
  | year = 2001
  | doi = 10.1137/S1064827500366124
  | bibcode = 2001SJSC...23..517K
 }}
</ref> Knyazev's implementation of [[LOBPCG]] is available in many open source software packages, e.g., [[BLOPEX]],  [[SciPy]], and [[ABINIT]].<ref>{{Citation
  | last1 = Bottin
  | first1 = F.
  | last2 = Leroux
  | first2 = S.
  | last3 = Knyazev
  | first3 = A.
  | last4 = Zerah
  | first4 = G.
  | title = Large scale ab initio calculations based on three levels of parallelization
  | journal = Computational Materials Science
  | volume = 42
  | issue = 2
  | pages = 329–336
  | year = 2008
  | doi = 10.1016/j.commatsci.2007.07.019
  | arxiv = 0707.3405
  | s2cid = 6206246
 }}
</ref>

Knyazev collaborated with [[John E. Osborn (mathematician)|John Osborn]]
<ref>{{Citation
  | last1 = Knyazev
  | first1 = A.V.
  | last2 = Osborn
  | first2 = J.
  | title = New A Priori FEM Error Estimates for Eigenvalues
  | journal = SIAM J. Numer. Anal.
  | volume = 43
  | issue = 6
  | pages = 2647–2667
  | year = 2006
  | doi = 10.1137/040613044
  }}
</ref>
on the theory of the [[Ritz method]] in the [[finite element method]] context 
and with [[Nikolai Sergeevich Bakhvalov]] ({{langx|ru|[[:ru:Бахвалов, Николай Сергеевич|Николай Серге́евич Бахвалов]]}}) ([[Erdős number]] 3 via [[Leonid Kantorovich]]) on numerical solution of [[elliptic partial differential equations]] with large jumps in the main coefficients.<ref>{{Citation
  | last1 = Bakhvalov
  | first1 = N.S.
  | last2 = Knyazev
  | first2 = A.V.
  | last3 = Parashkevov
  | first3 = R.R.
  | title = Extension Theorems for Stokes and Lamé equations for nearly incompressible media and their applications to numerical solution of problems with highly discontinuous coefficients
  | journal = Numerical Linear Algebra with Applications
  | volume = 9
  | issue = 2
  | pages = 115–139
  | year = 2002
  | doi = 10.1002/nla.259
  | s2cid = 14266720
 }}
</ref>
Jointly with his Ph.D. students, Knyazev pioneered using [[majorization]] for bounds in the [[Rayleigh–Ritz method]]
(see<ref>{{Citation
  | last1 = Knyazev
  | first1 = A.V.
  | last2 = Argentati
  | first2 = M.E.
  | title = Rayleigh–Ritz majorization error bounds with applications to FEM
  | journal = SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl.
  | volume = 31
  | issue = 3
  | pages = 1521–1537
  | year = 2010
  | doi = 10.1137/08072574X
  | arxiv = math/0701784
  | s2cid = 1390330
 }}
</ref> and references there) and contributed to the theory of [[angles between flats]].<ref>{{Citation
  | last1 = Knyazev
  | first1 = A.V.
  | last2 = Argentati
  | first2 = M.E.
  | title = Majorization for Changes in Angles Between Subspaces, Ritz Values, and Graph Laplacian Spectra
  | journal = SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl.
  | volume = 29
  | issue = 1
  | pages = 15–32
  | year = 2006
  | doi = 10.1137/060649070
  | arxiv = math/0508591
  | s2cid = 16987402
 }}</ref>
<ref>{{Citation
  | last1 = Knyazev
  | first1 = A.V.
  | last2 = Jujunashvili
  | first2 = A.
  | last3 = Argentati
  | first3 = M.E.
  | title = Angles between infinite dimensional subspaces with applications to the Rayleigh–Ritz and alternating projectors methods
  | journal = Journal of Functional Analysis
  | volume = 259
  | issue = 6
  | pages = 1323–1345
  | year = 2010
  | doi = 10.1016/j.jfa.2010.05.018
